items.title: Docs/site review follow-up: consolidate benchmark numbers, merge ADR trees, fix page metadata
items.body:
Follow-up to a documentation/website/UX review of the current version. The theme throughout: numbers and status claims were maintained in several places at once and had drifted apart after the 1.4/1.5 releases. This PR removes the duplication so each fact has one source of truth, and fixes the technical issues the review surfaced.

## Benchmark numbers: one source of truth

- `docs/proof-and-benchmarks.md` and `README.md` no longer quote their own (stale, mutually inconsistent) copies of the e2e workflow medians — they link the checked report `benchmarks/e2e-workflow/results/latest.md` and `docs/benchmark-e2e-workflow.md` instead.
- The website compare page derives its medians from `site/app/data/bench.ts`, which the existing `verify-site-bench-data.mjs` guard already asserts against the checked report — so the previously drifted "174 ms / 2254 ms" cells can no longer go stale. Hero/ProofStrip ratios come from the same guarded data.
- Fixed the compare criterion label (the cited numbers are from the realistic corpus, not the small one) and the Ferrocat version note (2.2.0, matching the pinned crate).

## ADR trees merged

`docs/adr/` (001/002, added 2026-07-22) collided with the canonical `adr/` series (001–016), claimed canonical status in parallel, and was never published to the website — the hosted CLI plugin API pages linked into a void. The plugin ADRs are now `adr/017` and `adr/018`, `DECISIONS.md` indexes them, links on the API pages resolve to live `/decisions/*` routes, and hardcoded "16 ADRs" counts were either removed or (on the site) derived at build time.

## Website fixes

- **Missing page metadata (SEO):** ~120 of 126 prerendered routes had no `<title>`, description, canonical, or OG tags. Root cause: Ardo 4 injects meta in an `enforce: "pre"` transform that looks for the compiled `export const frontmatter` in *raw* markdown, so it never fires. A small post-phase Vite plugin in `site/vite.config.ts` now injects the meta export after MDX compilation (and becomes a no-op if Ardo fixes the ordering upstream). Verified in the build output.
- **Hosting matrix:** `matrix.ts` claimed Remix subdomain demos were live (they are not hosted). It now matches `docs/demo-deployments.md`: cookie, route, and subdomain live for the five browser-verified frameworks; tld stays `provisioning` (domains not provisioned yet); Remix cells link the verified source. The `/frameworks` prose and per-framework panels agree with the table on the same page, and the deployment doc intro now states the tld status unambiguously.
- **Derived stats:** ADR count and example-matrix shape ("24 apps", "6 × 4") are generated into `content-stats.json` during prebuild instead of hardcoded — on the home page and the frameworks page.
- Removed the stale checked-in `sitemap.xml` (6 URLs, shadowed by the generated 126-URL one) and duplicate `robots.txt`; the get-started "Read the docs" CTA now points at `/docs` instead of the API reference; blog lede extraction no longer uses "Status: draft" as the meta description.

## Docs fixes

- `examples/README.md`: all 29 root-relative links resolved to 404 on GitHub (`examples/examples/…`); now correctly relative. Same class of fix in `docs/demo-deployments.md`.
- Contradictory "five vs. six framework families" wording unified everywhere: six families, five browser-verified, Remix v3 smoke-verified.
- README no longer claims Remix is verified on Node `>=22.22` (the package requires `>=24.3`), and its 30-link "Proof And Adoption Docs" farm is reduced to the website entry points plus a handful of repo anchors.
- Quickstart (`first-working-translation.md`) now works from an empty directory: scaffold step, `react`/`react-dom`/`solid-js` in the install lines.
- `benchmark-lingui-v6-preview.md` no longer lists `msg`/`defineMessage` as covered syntax (removed from Palamedes in 1.5.0); `migrate-from-lingui.md` no longer shows a module-level `t()` call that the documented scope rule forbids.
- `llms.txt`/`llms-full.txt` catch up on the Remix adapter, the CLI plugin system, and ADR 017/018.

## API reference corrections

- `transform.md`: four catalog-loader helper signatures were outdated (e.g. `renderCatalogModule(artifact, options)` vs. the real `renderCatalogModule(messages)`); export list completed.
- `config.md`: documents `loadPalamedesConfigSync` (used by the Remix register hook).
- `core.md`: `getMessageNodes()` added to the `PalamedesI18n` snippet (custom implementations failed typecheck without it); missing node types listed.
- `remix.md`: `PalamedesRemixRegisterOptions` now shows `configPath`/`failOnMissing`/`failOnCompileError`; server accessor `get()` and the remaining `createRemixI18nServer` options documented.
- `runtime.md`: lists `ClientI18nSnapshot`.

## Verification

- `pnpm --filter @palamedes/site build` — green, including the bench drift guard, prebuild, Ardo link check (`level: "error"`), and prerender of all routes (now 128 with the two new decision pages). Spot-checked titles/canonical/OG in the built HTML and the rewritten `/decisions/017…` links on the hosted API pages.
- `pnpm --filter @palamedes/site typecheck`, `pnpm lint` (oxlint + eslint), `pnpm format:check` — all green.
- Greptile review findings (tld cells wrongly live, duplicated matrix counts) addressed in 9405053.

## Known issue, deliberately not fixed here

## Summary

This PR updates all documentation files to reflect the current state of the Rust-based `caspar-node` implementation (v0.1.0) and the measured performance from the `reports/final` benchmark run (2026-05-29). The documentation now accurately describes the architecture, setup, and operational characteristics of the production codebase.

## Key Changes

- **ARCHITECTURE.md**: Completely restructured to document the Rust node topology, startup composition, core subsystems (action router, core transactions, Babble chain, VM manager, storage drivers, telemetry), the creature programming model, multi-runtime VM router, elpify-chain STARK validator election, federation, sharding, and security model. Replaced outdated Go-centric descriptions with current Rust implementation details.

- **README.md**: Refreshed to emphasize the unified Rust codebase (no Go toolchain required), clarified the creature programming model and multi-runtime execution, added measured performance metrics from the final benchmark run (10.5 ops/s peak throughput, ≈95 ms median consensus round, 100% correctness across 154 test steps), and updated repository map to reflect current structure (`node/`, `cmd/casparctl/`, `sdk/`, `reports/`).

- **BENCHMARKS.md** (new): Added comprehensive benchmark documentation including setup details, correctness results (154/154 steps, 100% pass rate), sequential throughput metrics (peak 10.50 ops/s on `chain:submitBaseTrx`), latency percentiles, elpify-chain election phase breakdown, mixed workload results, concurrent load testing (MASM peaks at 11.31 proofs/s @ C=2), and scope notes on shard independence and scalability.

- **GETTING_STARTED.md**: Updated prerequisites to reflect Rust-only build (removed Go 1.24.x requirement), clarified storage migration from Badger to RocksDB with QuestDB for telemetry, updated build instructions to use `make build` and Cargo, added `run-nodes.sh` quick-start flow, and expanded operational notes.

- **API_REFERENCE.md**: Clarified frame tag byte meanings, added explicit consensus routing rules (origin field determines chain ordering), and noted that binary blob I/O currently uses the binary action protocol rather than dedicated HTTPS endpoints.

- **CONSENSUS_NOTES.md**: Added verification note against the current Rust Babble port with measured latency/throughput references to BENCHMARKS.md.

## Notable Details

- All timestamps updated to 2026-05-29 to reflect the final benchmark run.
- Documentation now consistently refers to the Rust implementation as the authoritative version; `node.old/` is noted as legacy reference only.
- Performance metrics are tied to `reports/final/` as the source of truth.

items.body:
## Summary

This PR focuses `kadireren7/membrane` on the maintained implementation, moving active research ownership to the new public repository [`kadireren7/membrane-research`](https://github.com/kadireren7/membrane-research).

## Why

As MEMBRANE's research record grew (full phased experiment histories, simulators, a paper, an outreach package), it made this repository harder to navigate for its actual purpose: building and using the maintained implementation. The maintained implementation and the research record also have genuinely different lifecycles. See `docs/repository-boundary.md`'s "The two-repository decision" section for the full account, including why this revisits (not silently overturns) an earlier, deliberate decision to keep everything in one repository.

## What moved

301 files, SHA256-verified, already committed and pushed to `kadireren7/membrane-research`: `EXP-FPGA-DIV-001` and `EXP-FPGA-DIV-002`'s full research records, exploratory RTL (`rtl/experimental/`, imported from both `experiment/q8-divider-pipeline` and the previously-orphaned `experiment/fp-divider-pipeline`), research simulators, the paper, and the outreach package. Full provenance: `kadireren7/membrane-research`'s own `provenance/import-manifest.json` and `source-map.md`.

## What this PR actually removes from `membrane`

Only 51 files — the subset a real dependency audit (`migration/removal-dependency-check.json`, generated in this PR) confirmed has **no** maintained-build, maintained-test, or maintained-CI dependency: `experiments/EXP-FPGA-DIV-001/**`, `outreach/**` + `scripts/verify-outreach.py`, `tools/membrane-fpga-runtime/**`, and `rtl/tb/tb_q8_scale.sv`.

**Real finding, not assumed**: the same audit found the original migration inventory's classification of `tools/membrane-kv-*`, `benchmarks/**`, and `paper/**` as "research-only" was wrong for this repository's purposes — all three are wired into the maintained CMake build, maintained tests (`tests/unit`'s `test_interrupted_resume` needs a real `benchmarks/cxl-sim/` trace file), or maintained CI (`.github/workflows/paper.yml`). **None of the three is removed here.** `docs/phase*.md` is retained too — `docs/results-summary.md` (a maintained document) and multiple maintained source-code comments cite it throughout; severing that safely needs a dedicated follow-up pass, not a rushed one here.

## What stayed, and why (see README.md's own "Repository layout")

`tools/`, `benchmarks/`, `paper/`, and `docs/` still contain research-flavored material by subject matter — they stay because the maintained build/tests/CI genuinely depend on them, not because they were missed.

## No research data lost

Every removed file is already present, SHA256-verified, in `kadireren7/membrane-research` before removal here — confirmed via that repository's own `scripts/verify-provenance.py` (301/301 entries verified) prior to this PR being opened.

## README / reproduction

- `README.md`: 300 → 196 lines. Portfolio-focused: maintained-components table, 6-row verified-results table (Q8_0 result explicitly labeled RESEARCH ONLY), quick start, project status split, prominent limitations, two-repository explanation, honest AI-assisted-development section.
- `docs/reproduction.md`: trimmed to the maintained flow only, plus a pointer to `kadireren7/membrane-research`'s own full guide. **Found and fixed a real, pre-existing bug** while verifying this end to end: the Verilator cosimulation command was missing two RTL files (`membrane_fp_divider_radix4.sv`, `membrane_fp_scale_neg_pow2.sv`) `q4_scale.sv` has required since the `EXP-FPGA-DIV-001` promotion — confirmed broken, then fixed, by actually running it.
- `CONTRIBUTING.md`: explicit product-vs-research contribution paths; `experiment/*` branches no longer start here (existing ones preserved, unchanged, and mirrored into the research repo).

## Verification (all run on this branch, this session)

|---|---|
| Configure + build (Release) | Clean |
| `ctest` (Release) | 28/28 passed |
| ASan+UBSan | 28/28 passed |

## Safety

- **`third_party/llama.cpp` untouched** — same pre-existing dirty submodule state as before this branch, confirmed via `git diff --stat` (0 changes).

items.title: Consolidate examples and reproducible paper workflows
items.body:
## Summary

This PR has two related goals:

1. Establish a common publication style for figures across the paper.
2. Make the code, data, and outputs underlying paper results discoverable and reproducible.

The visual work is the primary user-facing change. Plotters for Sections IVa, IVb, Va, Vc, Vd, Ve, and Vf now share the same Matplotlib style foundation and use paper-oriented dimensions, typography, line treatment, labels, legends, and export settings.

The repository changes support that work by moving paper-specific workflows out of general examples and benchmark utilities into section-owned directories under `paper_results/`.

## Common paper figure style

This PR adds `paper_results/paper.mplstyle` and applies it across the revised paper plotters. The shared style defines the baseline serif and mathematical typography, grid appearance, legend frames, axis and tick treatment, default line width, and export bounding box.

Each plotter retains local control over figure-specific requirements such as physical size, aspect ratio, DPI, colors, and panel layout. This keeps the common layer small while aligning the visible conventions that should be consistent across the paper.

The revised plotters use:

- figure sizes specified in physical units for paper-column layouts;
- consistent serif and mathematical typography;
- explicit axis labels with physical units;
- deliberate colors and line styles for coordinates, controllers, references, and baselines;
- prominent reference trajectories where close tracking would otherwise obscure them;
- compact legends and layouts suitable for the manuscript;
- noninteractive CLI options for automated figure generation;
- paper-ready PDF outputs, with PNG or video outputs where the workflow needs them.

Section Vc receives additional plot-specific work:

- The configuration-space paper figure compares the controller trajectories directly and reports RMSE separately for the setpoint and trajectory-reference phases.
- RMSE panels identify the generalized configurations or strains represented by each value.
- The operational-space paper figure presents the partial-feedback-linearization rollout in a compact position/orientation layout.
- A separate saved-data workflow provides the full-versus-partial feedback-linearization analysis without coupling it to the canonical paper figure.
- Desired trajectories use increased line width and drawing order so they remain visible under closely matching actual trajectories.

The PR also adds composed paper outputs under `paper_results/final_outputs/` for the figures that combine or arrange section-level results.

## Paper reproduction structure

Paper workflows are organized by paper section. Each case keeps its generation or simulation code alongside its input or generated data and documented outputs. Reproduction commands and artifact mappings are provided by the root paper-results index and the section READMEs that are included:

```text
paper_results/<section>/
├── code/
├── data/
├── outputs/
└── README.md  # where the section has dedicated reproduction documentation
```

Paths are resolved from the owning script or case directory rather than the caller's working directory. Migrated CLIs expose input and output paths, create destination directories when needed, support noninteractive plotting, and protect existing outputs where appropriate.

Section data and paper outputs are stored as regular Git objects; trained Section Vf checkpoints use Git LFS. Validation runs use temporary destinations so they do not replace the committed paper artifacts.

## Net changes from `main`

### Section IVa: sequential CPU comparison

- Renames `paper_results/benchmarking_sequential_cpu/` to the paper-section-oriented `secIVa_benchmarking_sequential_cpu/`.
- Keeps the existing SoRoMoX, PyElastica, and SoRoSim generators and datasets with the owning paper result.
- Reworks the rollout comparison plotter to use the common paper style.
- Adds section documentation and refreshed paper outputs.

### Section IVb: parallel GPU rollouts

- Moves the batch-scaling generator and plotter from `tools/benchmarks/` into `paper_results/secIVb_parallel_rollouts_gpu/`.
- Moves the corresponding CSV data out of the top-level `benchmarks/batch_scaling/` directory.
- Adds standardized scaling, combined-scaling, and throughput figures.
- Leaves reusable system-method and derivative-path diagnostics in `tools/benchmarks/`.

### Section Va: system identification

- Moves the soft-tentacle parameter and residual-identification workflows from `examples/system_identification/` into `paper_results/secVa_system_identification/`.
- Adds the plotting workflow, supporting data, four paper figures, and reproduction documentation.

### Section Vc: model-based control

- Moves the configuration-space comparison from `examples/control/configuration_space/` into its own paper case.
- Moves the operational-space impedance example from `examples/control/operational_space/` into a separate paper case.
- Adds saved NPZ trajectories, case-specific plotting and rendering entry points, dedicated READMEs, and the committed `configuration_space_comparison.pdf`, `regulation_tracking_rmse.pdf`, and `operational_space_impedance_control.pdf` paper figures.
- Separates data generation, plotting, and rendering so figures and videos can be reproduced without rerunning simulations.

### Section Vd: control-gain optimization

- Moves the collocated and synergistic optimization workflows and their data from `examples/optimization/` into `paper_results/secVd_control_gain_optimization/`.
- Adds case-relative paths, CLI controls, documentation, and the standardized paper figure.

### Section Ve: safety-constrained control

- Replaces the single example entry point with separate generation, shared-control, plotting, and video-rendering modules under `paper_results/secVe_safety_constrained_control/`.
- Adds saved rollouts, system parameters, snapshots, and the paper plot outputs.

### Section Vf: parallel reinforcement learning

- Moves the RL environment, training, evaluation, policy rollout, checkpoints, and reward logs from `examples/control/rl/` into `paper_results/secVf_parallel_rl/`.
- Adds an offline video renderer, saved rollout and snapshot data, a standardized reward plot, and reproduction documentation.

## Examples and development benchmarks

The remaining examples stay focused on lightweight demonstrations. Their generated figures and videos are written to example-local artifact directories instead of the repository root, and `examples/README.md` documents the resulting structure.

The benchmark system registry is updated to use the current typed parameter APIs for Pendulum, articulated robot, planar PCS, PCS, and GVS systems. Tests cover each registered system and the GVS basis-order configuration. The outdated dictionary constructors are also present on the PR base, so this repairs an existing benchmark issue rather than a regression caused by the reorganization.

## Documentation and artifact handling

- Replaces `paper_results/README.txt` with a section and artifact index in `paper_results/README.md`.
- Updates the root README, examples guide, benchmark documentation, and changelog.
- Keeps trained Section Vf checkpoints in Git LFS; Section Vc data, figures, and video are regular Git objects.
- Removes generated caches and superseded benchmark images from their former locations.

## Validation

- Section Vc test suite: **70 passed**
- Focused migration and benchmark tests: **76 passed**
- Full local suite excluding the Viser live-mode shutdown case: **1191 passed, 1 deselected**
- Ruff passes for the changed Python files.
- Revised plotters were run noninteractively and checked for dimensions, panel structure, labels, legends, line visibility, and output creation.
- Migrated workflows were exercised from unrelated working directories to verify case-relative paths.
- Plotting tests use temporary schema-complete inputs and do not require Git LFS hydration in CI.
- Review follow-up tests cover automatic Open3D viewer shutdown and the disableable RL trajectory overlay.

## Reproduction limitations observed

- The UMArm Viser live-mode smoke test hangs during server-thread shutdown in the local environment.
- The Section Va neural-network residual prediction does not reproduce the committed RMSE, although the geometry and optimal-residual paths agree to numerical precision.
- The Section Vd collocated optimization develops steady-state velocity and subsequently NaNs under the committed scientific settings.
- Full GPU timing reproduction, MATLAB/SoRoSim execution, full RL retraining, and interactive video integrations require hardware or external runtimes that were not available for the complete validation run.

No scientific parameters, gains, seeds, datasets, or benchmark definitions were changed merely to force agreement.

items.title: [Benchmarks] Improve run-to-run benchmark consistency
items.body:
## Description 

This PR aims to improve run-to-run benchmark consistency, meaning runs with the exact same parameters and kernel implementations should report more or less the same execution time. Tighter numbers allow for more informed analysis of future kernel optimizations.

This also includes better documentation for the benchmark testing methodology, and how to best interpret results.

## Technical Details
- Removes the outdated graphing script since the output format has changed drastically.
- Updates the benchmark README with new instructions and a section on benchmark testing methodology.
- GPU operators now use HIP event timing to include the kernel time only, which prevents stream synchronization/kernel launch overhead from adding noise. Though these numbers are not as realistic, they prove more useful for actual implementation level optimizations.
- The C++ benchmarking binary now outputs each run separately instead of aggregating results into a single row. Analysis is moved to a new python script instead.
- Adds a python script (`benchmarks/analyze_results.py`) which analyzes the raw data exported from the benchmarking binary. It offers several strategies for filtering outliers. These results can be exported into a cleaned up CSV with raw results for each benchmark unit aggregated into a single row.

This PR contains the following updates:

| Package | Type | Update | Change | OpenSSF |

---

### Release Notes

<details>
<summary>ultralytics/ultralytics (ultralytics)</summary>

### [`v8.4.84`](https://redirect.github.com/ultralytics/ultralytics/releases/tag/v8.4.84): - Fix EMA-NaN no-checkpoint loss and unhelpful imgsz error (#​25005)

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/ultralytics/ultralytics/compare/v8.4.83...v8.4.84)

#### 🌟 Summary

Ultralytics `v8.4.84` improves training reliability, OBB stability, RT-DETR benchmarking accuracy, and LiteRT/mobile deployment documentation, with the most important fix ensuring valid training runs still save checkpoints even after transient NaN/Inf events 🚀

#### 📊 Key Changes

- **More reliable checkpoint saving during training** 🛡️\
  Fixed a production issue where training could complete successfully but fail at the end because no `best.pt` or `last.pt` checkpoint was saved. This happened when transient NaN/Inf values contaminated the EMA model state.

- **Cleaner `imgsz` validation errors** 🧭\
  Invalid image size strings like `imgsz=640x480` now raise a clear `ValueError` explaining the correct formats, instead of exposing a raw Python parsing error.

- **Improved OBB training stability for tiny rotated boxes** 📦\
  Added safer handling in rotated bounding box loss calculations by applying a small floor inside probabilistic IoU covariance calculations. This helps prevent loss divergence when training on very small oriented objects.

- **Fixed RT-DETR benchmark validation after export** 📈\
  Exported RT-DETR models are now reloaded with the correct `RTDETR` wrapper during benchmarking instead of `YOLO`, ensuring the proper validator and postprocessing are used. This fixes cases where benchmark mAP incorrectly showed `0`.

- **Axelera YOLO11 segmentation example improvements** 🎥\
  The `examples/YOLO-Axelera-Python/yolo11-seg.py` example now handles numeric camera sources correctly by mapping them to `/dev/video<N>` and using the OpenCV backend. Single-image sources also keep the display window open properly.

- **LiteRT and mobile deployment docs expanded** 📱\
  Documentation now highlights the official [Ultralytics YOLO Flutter plugin](https://redirect.github.com/ultralytics/yolo-flutter-app) for running LiteRT `.tflite` exports on Android, including real-time camera inference, single-image prediction, GPU acceleration, and YOLO26 task support.

- **New LiteRT performance guidance** ⚡\
  Added measured Android LiteRT performance tables for YOLO26n models across detection, segmentation, semantic segmentation, classification, pose, and OBB tasks, helping users understand real-world CPU/GPU mobile performance.

- **TensorFlow\.js and TF SavedModel docs updated** 🔗\
  Deprecated TensorFlow\.js export guidance now points to Google’s official [LiteRT.js web runtime documentation](https://developers.google.com/edge/litert/web), and TF SavedModel docs consistently refer to LiteRT instead of TensorFlow Lite where appropriate.

- **Documentation tooling maintenance** 🧰\
  Updated the MkDocs Ultralytics plugin requirement to `>=0.2.5` and added missing GitHub author metadata.

#### 🎯 Purpose & Impact

- **Fewer failed training jobs** ✅\
  Users are less likely to lose completed training runs due to checkpoint-saving failures. Even if a temporary numerical issue appears in EMA/model tensors, Ultralytics now sanitizes the saved checkpoint instead of ending with no persistent weights.

- **Better user experience for configuration mistakes** 💬\
  Clearer `imgsz` errors make it easier for both beginners and advanced users to fix incorrect command-line or Python arguments quickly.

- **More stable OBB model training** 🧱\
  Datasets with tiny rotated objects should train more reliably, reducing the chance of unstable gradients or diverging losses in oriented bounding box workflows.

- **Trustworthy RT-DETR benchmark results** 🎯\
  RT-DETR users should now see meaningful benchmark metrics after export instead of misleading zero-mAP results caused by the wrong validation pipeline.

- **Smoother edge and mobile deployment path** 📲\
  The LiteRT documentation improvements make it easier to choose the right deployment route for Android, browser, Apple, and Qualcomm NPU targets, especially with YOLO26 as the recommended model family.

- **Improved examples and docs reduce friction** 🙌\
  Axelera users get a more practical segmentation demo, while documentation updates help deployment users avoid dead links, outdated terminology, and unclear driver-version issues.

#### What's Changed

- Fix --source camera handling and single-image display in yolo11-seg example by [@​tatsuya-toyoda](https://redirect.github.com/tatsuya-toyoda) in [#​24969](https://redirect.github.com/ultralytics/ultralytics/pull/24969)
- fix: RTDETR benchmark mAP=0 in benchmark by [@​artest08](https://redirect.github.com/artest08) in [#​24998](https://redirect.github.com/ultralytics/ultralytics/pull/24998)
- Bump MkDocs plugin requirement by [@​glenn-jocher](https://redirect.github.com/glenn-jocher) in [#​25002](https://redirect.github.com/ultralytics/ultralytics/pull/25002)
- Fix LiteRT.js documentation link by [@​glenn-jocher](https://redirect.github.com/glenn-jocher) in [#​25000](https://redirect.github.com/ultralytics/ultralytics/pull/25000)
- Add mobile-apps notice to LiteRT docs and finish TF SavedModel LiteRT rename by [@​glenn-jocher](https://redirect.github.com/glenn-jocher) in [#​25004](https://redirect.github.com/ultralytics/ultralytics/pull/25004)
- Fix sub-stride OBB loss divergence via probiou floor by [@​lmycross](https://redirect.github.com/lmycross) in [#​25007](https://redirect.github.com/ultralytics/ultralytics/pull/25007)
- Fix EMA-NaN no-checkpoint loss and unhelpful imgsz error by [@​glenn-jocher](https://redirect.github.com/glenn-jocher) in [#​25005](https://redirect.github.com/ultralytics/ultralytics/pull/25005)

#### New Contributors

- [@​tatsuya-toyoda](https://redirect.github.com/tatsuya-toyoda) made their first contribution in [#​24969](https://redirect.github.com/ultralytics/ultralytics/pull/24969)

**Full Changelog**: <https://github.com/ultralytics/ultralytics/compare/v8.4.83...v8.4.84>

### [`v8.4.83`](https://redirect.github.com/ultralytics/ultralytics/releases/tag/v8.4.83): - New Google LiteRT export replaces legacy TFLite and TF.js (#​22870)

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/ultralytics/ultralytics/compare/v8.4.82...v8.4.83)

#### 🌟 Summary

🚀 **Ultralytics v8.4.83 is led by a major export upgrade: the new Google LiteRT format now replaces the older separate TFLite and TF.js export paths, while several reliability and performance fixes make training, segmentation, and deployment more stable.**

#### 📊 Key Changes

- 🔄 **New LiteRT export replaces legacy TFLite and TF.js workflows**
  - Added a new `format="litert"` export option.
  - LiteRT becomes the **unified path** for mobile, edge, embedded, and browser deployment.
  - Legacy `tflite` and `tfjs` names still work, but now show deprecation warnings and redirect to LiteRT.
  - Added a dedicated LiteRT backend so exported `.tflite` models can be loaded for **predict** and **val** inside Ultralytics.

- 📱 **Broader on-device deployment support**
  - LiteRT uses Google’s newer runtime direction for `.tflite` models.
  - Supports multiple quantization modes, including:
    - standard INT8
    - mixed INT8 + 16-bit activations
    - dynamic INT8 without calibration data
  - This makes exports more flexible for mobile and edge hardware.

- 🌐 **Browser deployment is simplified**
  - Instead of needing a separate TF.js export, browser use is now handled through **LiteRT.js** with the same `.tflite` model.
  - This reduces duplication and makes web deployment easier to understand.

- 🧠 **Segmentation memory use and speed improved**
  - Segmentation mask post-processing was optimized to reduce peak memory use and speed up execution.
  - This helps avoid out-of-memory failures on large images or high-object-count scenes.

- 🛡️ **Training checkpoint reliability improved**
  - Fixed a long-standing issue where a bad EMA state could prevent **any checkpoint** from being saved.
  - Training runs are now less likely to fail at the finish line because of temporary numerical issues.

- ⚡ **Mixed-precision attention made safer**
  - Attention computations were reordered to reduce FP16 overflow risk.
  - This helps prevent `inf`/`nan` problems during AMP or half-precision training.

- 🧹 **Multi-dataset and dataloader memory/file-handle fixes**
  - MultiTrainer now avoids retaining large trainer objects unnecessarily.
  - DataLoader reset now properly shuts down old workers, preventing “too many open files” errors in long runs.

- 🎯 **Classification INT8 calibration improved**
  - Classification exports now use a classification-specific dataset pipeline for INT8 calibration rather than detection-style loading.
  - This should produce more correct and robust classification quantized exports.

- ✅ **Better dataset validation**
  - Segment tasks now fail early if users accidentally provide box-only labels instead of segmentation labels.
  - This prevents confusing downstream errors later in validation or training.

- 🌍 **YOLO-World distributed training fix**
  - Class setup is now applied on all DDP ranks, improving consistency in multi-GPU training.

#### 🎯 Purpose & Impact

- **For mobile, edge, and web developers** 📦\
  LiteRT is the biggest change in this release. It simplifies deployment by replacing two older export formats with **one modern, unified export flow**. That means less confusion, fewer export branches, and a cleaner path from training to deployment.

- **For teams shipping browser apps** 🌐\
  You no longer need to think of browser support as a separate TF.js pipeline. A single LiteRT `.tflite` model can now cover both on-device and web use cases more cleanly.

- **For users exporting quantized models** ⚙️\
  The added LiteRT quantization options offer more choices for balancing size, speed, and accuracy, especially on constrained hardware.

- **For training stability** 🛠️\
  Several fixes reduce frustrating failures:
  - fewer broken checkpoints
  - fewer FP16 numerical issues
  - fewer leaked workers and file descriptors
  - more reliable multi-dataset training

- **For segmentation users** 🎭\
  Lower memory usage and faster mask processing can make segmentation inference more practical on larger inputs and reduce OOM crashes.

- **For dataset preparation** 🧾\
  Earlier validation catches common mistakes sooner, which saves debugging time and prevents invalid runs.

- **Overall impact** ✨\
  This release is especially valuable for anyone deploying YOLO26 to **mobile, embedded, edge, or browser environments**, while also improving everyday robustness for training and segmentation workloads.

#### What's Changed

- Linkify PR numbers in publish Slack notifications by [@​glenn-jocher](https://redirect.github.com/glenn-jocher) in [#​24966](https://redirect.github.com/ultralytics/ultralytics/pull/24966)
- Use ClassificationDataset for classify INT8 export calibration by [@​onuralpszr](https://redirect.github.com/onuralpszr) in [#​24972](https://redirect.github.com/ultralytics/ultralytics/pull/24972)

items.title: Feat/improve inter subject
items.body:
This pull request introduces several significant improvements and new features to the EEG training pipeline, focusing on data augmentation, training configuration, and reproducibility. The main highlights are the addition of a Gaussian smoothing EEG augmentation, a more flexible and robust learning rate schedule, and expanded reporting and configuration options.

**Key changes:**

### Data Augmentation

* Added a new EEG smoothing augmentation (`smooth_eeg`) that applies Gaussian smoothing along the time axis during training to reduce high-frequency noise and improve cross-subject generalization. This is configurable and only applied during training. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-234c33e51515af24cb656014bcc57bea562695530f7c9733ed94a8fcd845dd7dR1-R58) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-461d99129b58808bf9762b09df9319f55b4c22ada55645eb7eba72a3af29933fL210-R228)
* Integrated the smooth augmentation into the training loop, with new configuration parameters for probability, kernel size, and sigma. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-461d99129b58808bf9762b09df9319f55b4c22ada55645eb7eba72a3af29933fR182-R186) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-cc6ff10f70311db9bd57e102b0f7a2258df3266a18837e4489daa366210cb31bR52-R61)

### Training Configuration and Scheduling

* Introduced a new learning rate scheduler (`make_scheduler`) that performs a linear warmup followed by cosine annealing, replacing the previous two-stage manual learning rate and encoder freezing logic. This provides a smoother and more modern training schedule. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-461d99129b58808bf9762b09df9319f55b4c22ada55645eb7eba72a3af29933fR426-R461) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-cc6ff10f70311db9bd57e102b0f7a2258df3266a18837e4489daa366210cb31bL27-R36)
* Updated default training parameters: increased epochs to 200, batch size to 1024, eval every epoch, longer stage 1, lower final MMD weight, and more conservative stage 2 learning rate.

### Reproducibility and Reporting

* Expanded the results tables in `reports/experiment_baseline.md` to include more baselines and new augmentation results, improving transparency and benchmarking.
* Added documentation and logging for running training with `nohup` and log tailing in the `README.md`.

### Testing and Code Quality

* Added unit tests for the new `smooth_eeg` augmentation to ensure correct behavior and integration.
* Refactored and clarified model docstrings and removed outdated comments for improved readability. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-3ec6a4a9c2e9ecd56813c73e6a0d800df7308b40aa59f63e88b4f5c11d2b1020L112-R125) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-550dc7d6ff7022d4891b75f591fe72fcf14322554db20f2cc5bcd7e88c3d0a08L16-L18)

### Minor Adjustments

* Changed default for `data_average` to `false` for more realistic training.
* Updated the flowchart in the `README.md` to reflect the removal of encoder freezing in stage 2.

These changes collectively modernize the training pipeline, improve model generalization, and make experiments more reproducible and easier to configure.

items.title: Capture PhysX contact sensor kernels in CUDA graphs
items.body:
# Description

Reports came in that our stack is slow with PhysX, and profiling the contact sensor update confirmed that the eager `wp.launch` calls dominate its per-step CPU cost: a single eager launch of `update_net_forces_kernel` costs ~110 us of CPU submit time, while replaying the same kernel from a CUDA graph costs ~7 us. The PhysX tensor reads themselves are comparatively cheap (~34 us).

This PR captures the warp kernels of the PhysX `ContactSensor` buffer update into CUDA graphs on first use and replays them on subsequent updates:

- **PhysX tensor reads stay eager.** They cannot be captured — `GpuRigidContactView` enqueues its work on the legacy CUDA stream, and capture fails with `operation would make the legacy stream depend on a capturing blocking stream`. Fortunately the tensor API caches its output buffers and refreshes them in place on every call, so the getters run eagerly before each graph replay and the graphed kernels read the refreshed data.
- **Per-stage graphs.** `get_contact_data` and `get_friction_data` share their count/start-index buffers on the view, so each stage's kernel must run before the next stage's PhysX read. Each stage (net forces, pose, contact points, friction forces) is therefore captured as its own graph, preserving the exact ordering of the eager path.
- **Only graphs when not already being graphed.** If an outer CUDA graph capture is active (`device.is_capturing`), the kernels run "eagerly" and are recorded into that outer graph instead of replaying a nested one.
- **Safe fallbacks.** Eager execution on CPU devices; a one-time warning and permanent eager fallback if capture fails; graphs bake input pointers and are dropped/re-captured if a pointer changes; all graphs are dropped when the physics views are invalidated.

A new benchmark script compares the two paths:

```bash
./isaaclab.sh -p scripts/benchmarks/benchmark_contact_sensor.py --num_envs 4096 --headless
./isaaclab.sh -p scripts/benchmarks/benchmark_contact_sensor.py --num_envs 4096 --disable_graph --headless
```

Results on an RTX 5000 Ada laptop GPU (default sensor config: net forces + air time, 500 timed steps, mean synchronized update time):

| num_envs | eager | graphed |
|---|---|---|
| 32 | 0.463 ms | 0.407 ms |
| 4096 | 0.490 ms | 0.391 ms |

The saving matches one graphed kernel (the default config launches a single kernel per update); configs with `track_pose` / `track_contact_points` / `track_friction_forces` graph up to four. The remaining overhead is the base-class `update_timestamp_kernel` / `update_outdated_envs_kernel` launches in `SensorBase`, which are shared across backends and left for a follow-up.

## Type of change

- New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality)

- [x] I have made corresponding changes to the documentation

items.title: refactor: compose ArcForge skill layers
items.body:
## Summary

- Refactor ArcForge's composable skill system into clearer layered behavior: core toolkit, optional workflows, and harness/eval isolation.
- Reduce `arc-using` from global routing pressure to a bounded, task-fit router: skills are tools, not laws.
- Make SessionStart skill injection minimal and non-invasive so it does not override harness behavior or other skills.
- Harden eval mechanics for composable-skill non-regression testing, including explicit preflight skip, non-regression verdict policy, grader failure handling, and effective trial git boundaries.
- Add 9 focused eval scenarios plus coverage documentation for activation/non-activation, SessionStart isolation, plugin-dir isolation, and other-skill noninterference.

## Validation

- `npm test`
- `npm run lint`
- `git diff --check origin/main..HEAD`
- `node scripts/cli.js eval lint` for all 9 new composable-skill scenarios
- Manual git boundary check: `git -C <trialDir> rev-parse --show-toplevel` resolves to the trial dir

Notes:
- `npm run lint` exits 0 with existing warnings/info.
- Existing untracked local `.hermes/` metadata is intentionally not included.
- Legacy/outdated scenario corpus is intentionally out of scope for this PR; this PR adds focused scenarios for the composable skill refactor risks.

## Follow-up cleanup

- Added README scaffolding for `evals/results/`, `evals/reports/`, and `evals/benchmarks/`.
- Kept raw eval results ignored by git while allowing documentation for the results directory.
- Removed 27 invalid active scenarios that failed the current eval lint contract; 14 active scenarios remain and all pass `node scripts/cli.js eval lint <scenario>`.

### [`v1.27.0`](https://redirect.github.com/jdx/aube/releases/tag/v1.27.0): : access, git-repo build approvals, concurrent installs

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/jdx/aube/compare/v1.26.0...v1.27.0)

A feature release that adds an npm-style `aube access` command and Git-repository-scoped `allowBuilds` keys, tightens credential redaction on publish, fixes stale pnpm patch handling after re-resolve, and lays the groundwork for parallel embedded installs by making the explicit-install path fully reentrant.

#### Added

- **`aube access`** ([#​1012](https://redirect.github.com/jdx/aube/pull/1012) by [@​jdx](https://redirect.github.com/jdx)) — Manage registry package permissions from the CLI, modeled on npm and compatible with pnpm's forms. Subcommands cover `get status`, `list packages` / `list collaborators`, `ls packages [entity]` (pnpm-compatible), `set status=public|private`, `set mfa=none|publish|automation`, `grant <permission> <team> <package>`, and `revoke <team> <package>`. Requests use scoped-registry auth, honor `--otp` for MFA-protected mutations, cap response bodies, and produce distinct errors (`ERR_AUBE_ACCESS_ENTITY_NOT_FOUND` vs. plain 404). Supports `--json` for scripting alongside the human-readable default.

- **Git-repository build approvals** ([#​1010](https://redirect.github.com/jdx/aube/pull/1010) by [@​jdx](https://redirect.github.com/jdx)) — `allowBuilds` rules can now be keyed by a package plus a normalized Git repository URL (for example, `native-addon@git+<https repo url>`). The commit is intentionally omitted from the key so audited repositories can advance to new SHAs without re-approving each one. Exact per-source approvals and name-only registry approvals still work as before, and deny rules continue to win over allows. Repository rules are applied consistently across lifecycle execution, script jailing, ignored-build reporting, and install graph hashes.

- **`aube add --dangerously-allow-all-builds`** ([#​1016](https://redirect.github.com/jdx/aube/pull/1016) by [@​risu729](https://redirect.github.com/risu729)) — The broad build-approval flag was previously only accepted on `install`, so `aube add --global <pkg> --dangerously-allow-all-builds` (as used by mise) was rejected at parse time. The flag now works on `add`, is forwarded through local, filtered, and global add paths into the shared install pipeline, and conflicts explicitly with `--deny-build=<pkg>`. The override is invocation-scoped — it does not persist `dangerouslyAllowAllBuilds=true` to project config.

#### Fixed

- **Redact inline registry credentials in publish output** ([#​1009](https://redirect.github.com/jdx/aube/pull/1009) by [@​jdx](https://redirect.github.com/jdx)) — When a registry URL embeds credentials in the `user:secret@host` form, publish no longer echoes them raw. The "already published" error, the OIDC token-exchange failure wrapper, and the `--dry-run` "would PUT to …" line now pass URLs through `aube_util::url::redact_url`. Dry-run output is centralized in `dry_run_outcome_line`, with test coverage confirming scoped package targets redact inline auth while preserving the encoded path.

- **Ignore stale pnpm patch entries after re-resolve** ([#​1022](https://redirect.github.com/jdx/aube/pull/1022) by [@​jdx](https://redirect.github.com/jdx), fixes [#​1019](https://redirect.github.com/jdx/aube/issues/1019)) — On a non-frozen install that had to re-resolve, `overlay_metadata_from` was copying `patchedDependencies` from the previous `pnpm-lock.yaml`, so removed or wrong-version patches were still being applied and written back. Fresh-resolve now replaces `graph.patched_dependencies` with the workspace's current `read_patched_dependencies`, and the pnpm 11 hash-only scalar form is no longer misread as a file path. Bats coverage was added for both the pnpm 10 object form and the pnpm 11 hash-only form.

#### Changed

- **Reentrant explicit-directory installs** ([#​1026](https://redirect.github.com/jdx/aube/pull/1026) by [@​jdx](https://redirect.github.com/jdx)) — Removes the process-wide project-lock reentrancy flag that could let an install for project B skip its filesystem lock just because project A was already installing in the same process. Commands that chain into install (`add`, `remove`, `update`, filtered add, `ci`, `dedupe`) now hold an explicit `ProjectLock` guard and call `install::run_with_project_lock`. Dependency-chain diagnostics move from a global mutex to Tokio task-local state and propagate into spawned fetch and lifecycle tasks, so parallel installs no longer clobber each other's transitive error chains. `configure_script_settings` also only mutates global script config when scripts aren't disabled.

- **Per-install runtime and script-settings isolation** ([#​1027](https://redirect.github.com/jdx/aube/pull/1027) by [@​jdx](https://redirect.github.com/jdx)) — Building on [#​1026](https://redirect.github.com/jdx/aube/issues/1026), Node runtime selection and lifecycle-script settings are now scoped to each explicit install via nested task-local scopes (`runtime`, `aube_scripts`) instead of process-wide snapshots. Spawned fetch and dependency-lifecycle tasks inherit the owning install's context via `scope_current`. The install entry uses `run_scoped` and `Box::pin`s `run_inner` to avoid Tokio worker stack overflow when scopes stack, and `aube runtime set` now re-reads `package.json` and the lockfile-pinned runtime for its status line rather than trusting a possibly stale process cache. Non-install CLI commands continue to use the process-wide fallbacks. Together with [#​1026](https://redirect.github.com/jdx/aube/issues/1026), this is prerequisite groundwork for concurrent embedded installs to drop their addon-wide serialization mutex.

- **Refreshed benchmarks for v1.26.0** ([#​1002](https://redirect.github.com/jdx/aube/pull/1002) by [@​jdx](https://redirect.github.com/jdx)) — `benchmarks/results.json` and the README `BENCH_RATIOS` block regenerated on the hermetic Verdaccio registry against aube 1.26.0 and pnpm 11.10.0. Public ratios shift to \~3× Bun / \~6× pnpm on warm installs and \~3× Bun / \~28× pnpm on the repeat `install && test` case.

#### New Contributors

- [@​risu729](https://redirect.github.com/risu729) made their first contribution in [#​1016](https://redirect.github.com/jdx/aube/pull/1016)

**Full Changelog**: <https://github.com/jdx/aube/compare/v1.26.0...v1.27.0>

items.title: [bugfix] Support MIXED forward mode in TBO splitter for DP attention
items.body:
## Motivation

\`--enable-dp-attention\` together with \`--enable-mixed-chunk\` crashes
deterministically at the first chunked-prefill iteration that merges a
running decode. The combination is silently broken — there's no validation
in \`server_args.py\` rejecting it, but no scheduler iteration with
\`forward_mode = MIXED\` ever survives long enough to reach the model.

Under DP attention, \`prepare_mlp_sync_batch_raw\` (\`scheduler_dp_attn_mixin.py:187\`)
unconditionally calls \`TboDPAttentionPreparer.prepare_all_gather\`, which
calls \`compute_split_seq_index\` on the local batch's \`forward_mode\` —
**even when \`--enable-two-batch-overlap\` is off**. That function (and
its companion \`compute_split_token_index\`) only handled
\`EXTEND / TARGET_VERIFY / DECODE / IDLE / PREBUILT\` and raised
\`NotImplementedError\` for \`ForwardMode.MIXED\`.

Repro on the failing combination:

\`\`\`
File \"python/sglang/srt/managers/scheduler_dp_attn_mixin.py\", line 187, in prepare_mlp_sync_batch_raw
    local_can_run_tbo, local_forward_mode = tbo_preparer.prepare_all_gather(local_batch)
File \"python/sglang/srt/batch_overlap/two_batch_overlap.py\", line 398, in prepare_all_gather
    self.local_tbo_split_seq_index = compute_split_seq_index(
File \"python/sglang/srt/batch_overlap/two_batch_overlap.py\", line 94, in compute_split_seq_index
    raise NotImplementedError()
NotImplementedError
\`\`\`

## Modifications

Treat \`ForwardMode.MIXED\` like \`ForwardMode.EXTEND\` in both
\`compute_split_seq_index\` and \`compute_split_token_index\`. After
\`mix_with_running\`, the running-decode reqs are appended to
\`extend_lens\` as length-1 entries, so \`_split_extend_seqs\` and the
cumulative-sum split logic apply unchanged.

Two-line fix in \`python/sglang/srt/batch_overlap/two_batch_overlap.py\`.
Added a regression test \`TestDPAttentionMixedChunk\` in
\`test/registered/distributed/test_dp_attention.py\` that exercises
\`--enable-dp-attention --enable-mixed-chunk --chunked-prefill-size 256\`
on the existing 2-GPU CI suite.

**Out of scope:** \`--enable-two-batch-overlap\` + \`--enable-mixed-chunk\`
is still unsupported. \`OperationsStrategy.init_new_tbo\` →
\`_compute_moe_*_layer_operations_strategy_tbo\` in
\`batch_overlap/operations_strategy.py\` (lines 84, 163, 240) also raise
\`NotImplementedError\` on MIXED. Non-TBO setups never reach those paths
because \`can_run_tbo\` requires \`enable_two_batch_overlap=True\`. Happy
to extend in a follow-up if there's interest.

## Accuracy Tests

DeepSeek-Coder-V2-Lite-Instruct, \`--tp 2 --enable-dp-attention --dp 2 --enable-mixed-chunk --chunked-prefill-size 256\`,
gsm8k 200 examples / 128 threads:

\`\`\`
gsm8k_score = 0.795   (threshold: 0.6)
output_throughput = 1138 token/s
\`\`\`

Mixed batches confirmed in scheduler logs (\`Prefill batch ... #running-req: 36\`).

8/8 outputs on a separate hand-crafted long+short prompt mix exactly match
a \`--enable-dp-attention\` (no mixed_chunk) baseline run, indicating
correct cross-DP token routing under MIXED.

Local run had to substitute \`deepseek-coder-v2-lite\` (cached) for
\`lmsys/sglang-ci-dsv3-test\` (gated on this box) and use
\`--attention-backend triton --disable-cuda-graph\` (an outdated local
\`sgl-kernel\` install passes an unsupported \`out=\` kwarg to FA3). The
registered CI test does not include those overrides — CI will run with
the canonical FA3 + cuda graph configuration.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

N/A — bugfix on a previously crashing path.

## Checklist

- [ ] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [ ] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

items.body:
## Summary

Systematic accuracy pass over user-facing text: docs pages, Python docstrings, inline comments, and example code. 90 small, high-confidence corrections — no behavior changes, no restyling, no restructuring. Every fix was verified against the authoritative source before inclusion: actual code paths and signatures, `ultralytics/cfg/default.yaml`, dataset YAMLs, the YOLOv5 repository for legacy docs, and the Platform app for platform docs. Ambiguous or lower-confidence findings were deliberately left out to keep this reviewable.

## Correction categories

- **Broken examples**: MobileSAM box-prompt section used point prompts; SAM predictor snippet missing `import cv2`; `torch2coreml()` call missing required `classifier_names`; `YOLOEDetect`/`YOLOESegment` docstring examples passed text embeddings as a second positional arg; `prompt_inference` example unpacked 3 returns (returns 2); `Results.plot()` example called `.show()` on an ndarray; OBB tracking example used `tracker=True` on predict instead of `model.track()`; `check_cfg` docstring example raised instead of passing
- **Docs vs code mismatches**: `benchmark()` device/imgsz docs; DEEPX calibration default `coco8.yaml` and unsupported `fraction` advice; ExecuTorch FAQ contradicted its own Predict/Validate examples; settings table (`settings_version` 0.0.6, `tensorboard`/`wandb` default `False`); `batch` vs nonexistent `batch_size`; solutions CLI list missing `region`/`security`/`parking`; solution outputs save to `runs/solutions/exp`; analytics output 1280×720; detection fitness weights; `ObjectCropper` filenames; `make_divisible` rounds up; `process_mask` output resolution; pose val keypoints scale to model-input space; OBB loss comment `xywhr (b, h*w, 5)`; autobatch fit is linear, not log-space; `Colors` palette is not TABLEAU; `ConfusionMatrix` task values; `SolutionResults` image attr is `plot_im`
- **Format/coordinate precision**: `imgsz` lists are `[h, w]`; pose "3D keypoints" → keypoint visibility; normalized vs pixel keypoint coords; HSV comment BGR not RGB; `polygon2mask` flat 1D polygon input; semantic mask extension resolution; classify split roles (`train`/`val`, optional `test`)
- **Invalid CLI/flags**: `yolo export model=... format=...` key=value form; `yolo settings vscode_msg=False`; YOLOv5 docs advertised nonexistent `--amp` and `--close-mosaic` flags; YOLOv5 evolve output `runs/evolve/exp/hyp_evolve.yaml`; run dirs `exp2` not `exp-2`; CPU docker run without `--runtime=nvidia`; `hyp.VOC.yaml` not `hyp.finetune.yaml`
- **Wrong links/names**: FastSAM repo org (CASIA-IVA-Lab); `autosplit` moved to `reference/data/split`; race-conditions text linked to algorithmic-bias glossary; RT-DETR = Real-Time DEtection TRansformer; `no_goggle` class name; YOLOv8 Explore row missing OBB
- **Stale values**: YOLO26n-cls 71.4%/90.1%; SAHI slice defaults 512; examples retirement note; `README.zh-CN.md` pose mAP 71.6 and semantic reproduce command

## Changed areas

- `docs/en/**` — 36 files (models, datasets, guides, integrations, modes, platform, solutions, usage, quickstart, yolov5)
- `ultralytics/**` — 22 files (cfg, data, engine, models, nn, solutions, utils — docstrings/comments only; one return annotation corrected to match the documented return, no runtime changes)
- `examples/**` — 5 READMEs; `README.zh-CN.md`

## Validation

- `git diff --check` clean
- `python -m py_compile` passes on all 22 edited Python files
- Relative-link + code-fence integrity check across all 36 changed markdown files: 0 broken links, all fences balanced
- Platform docs verified against the Platform app; YOLOv5 docs verified against ultralytics/yolov5; vendor-dependent claims verified against current vendor docs

## 🛠️ PR Summary

<sub>Made with ❤️ by [Ultralytics Actions](https://www.ultralytics.com/actions)</sub>

### 🌟 Summary
📝 This PR is primarily a documentation and example cleanup update that improves accuracy, fixes outdated commands and references, and aligns docs with current Ultralytics behavior across YOLO26, datasets, exports, solutions, and utilities.

### 📊 Key Changes
- 📚 Updated many docs pages to correct outdated or misleading instructions, parameter names, defaults, and examples.
- 🎯 Refined dataset documentation:
  - Classification split structure now correctly emphasizes `train` + `val`, with `test` optional.
  - Pose format wording now describes visibility flags more clearly.
  - Semantic segmentation docs now better explain mask file handling and recommend lossless formats like `.png`/`.tiff`.
  - Minor dataset label fixes such as `no_goggle` in Construction-PPE.
- 🤖 Refreshed model and benchmark docs:
  - Updated YOLO26 classification accuracy numbers in ImageNet docs.
  - Corrected benchmark docs to state that `benchmark()` only supports square `imgsz`.
  - Fixed model YAML docs to reflect current `Detect` arguments and `torchvision.ops.` module resolution.
- 🛠️ Improved command and API examples across guides:
  - Fixed CLI syntax like `yolo export model=yolo26n.pt format=tflite` and `yolo settings vscode_msg=False`.
  - Replaced incorrect `batch_size` references with the actual `batch` argument.
  - Updated CoreML export example to include `classifier_names=None`.
  - Corrected autosplit import/reference paths.
- 🧠 Clarified training and validation behavior:

  - Several comments/docstrings now better explain pose scaling, mask processing, class weights, confusion matrix task types, and divisibility behavior.

  - DEEPX docs now use `coco8.yaml` as the calibration dataset default and simplify calibration wording.
  - ExecuTorch docs now state that exported models can be loaded with `YOLO()` in Python for inference/validation.
- ✂️ Refined SAM and MobileSAM examples:
  - MobileSAM examples now focus on box prompts instead of point prompts.

- 🔍 Included many small consistency fixes:

### 🎯 Purpose & Impact

The public-dataset evaluation narrative was outdated — only M5 was mentioned, and the evidence hierarchy was flat. This updates three docs to reflect the new ordered hierarchy (synthetic core → Favorita → Rossmann) while preserving all methodological caution language.

**`README.md`**
- `What THUNBIT is not` — tightened to reflect synthetic benchmarks + exploratory non-labeled public checks
- `Benchmark summary` — replaced M5 paragraph with two-bullet Favorita/Rossmann narrative; reinforces synthetic benchmarks as quantitative core
- `Current status` table — renamed row to "Public plausibility audits"; lists Favorita + Rossmann with no-formal-validation qualifier

**`docs/benchmarking.md`**
